title: Biomarkers as Predictors of Successful Weight Loss
summary:
People with severe obesity respond differently to treatment. While some benefit mainly from lifestyle intervention, others respond better to medication or bariatric surgery. At present, it is difficult to predict which treatment is most suitable for an individual patient.

The aim of this study is to investigate whether biological characteristics measured in blood or stool samples can help predict treatment success. Such biomarkers may support a more individualised selection of obesity treatment in the future.

Adults with severe obesity receiving treatment at the obesity centre of the University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein are invited to participate. Treatment is provided according to routine clinical practice and is independent of study participation. During routine visits, clinical data are documented and additional blood and stool samples are collected whenever blood sampling is already required for clinical care. All data and samples are analysed in pseudonymised form.
conditions: Class III obesity (BMI >40 kg/m²) and obesity-associated comorbidities, particularly type 2 diabetes mellitus and metabolic syndrome

interventions.name:
Prospective observation of adults with severe obesity receiving routine treatment at the interdisciplinary obesity centre of the University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein, Campus Kiel.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Written informed consent obtained prior to study participation
- Treatment at the interdisciplinary obesity centre of the University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein, Campus Kiel
- Clinical indication for established conservative, pharmacological or surgical obesity treatment
- Willingness to participate in scheduled study assessments and follow-up examinations
Exclusion criteria:
BMI <40 kg/m2
